summary: Requests that RFC 1403, BGP OSPF Interaction, be moved to Historic status because the technology is no longer used.

eli5.summary: It says an old rule for two route-sharing systems is unused and should be retired.

questions: why was bgp ospf interaction unused
subtitle: Retiring an unused BGP and OSPF interaction specification.

tldr.problem: RFC 1403 describes BGP OSPF interaction, a mechanism that adds significant implementation complexity but has never been deployed in the public internet.
tldr.mechanism: This document requests that RFC 1403 be reclassified as Historic status to indicate it is no longer recommended for use.
tldr.outcome: The specification remains available for historical reference, but implementations should not use this mechanism for connecting BGP and OSPF routing protocols.

today: RFC 1403 is now Historic. This RFC, 3166, documents that status change.

sections.title: An Unused Routing Interaction
sections.content:
RFC 1403 specified a way for BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) and OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing protocols to interact with each other. However, during a standards review, it became clear that this interaction is not in common use and may never have been deployed in the public internet.

The mechanism requires significant implementation complexity in routers, making it impractical without clear operational demand. Since no evidence of deployment exists after many years, reclassifying it as Historic is the appropriate action.
sections.eli5: Routers have two ways to share route information with each other. Someone designed a way for these two methods to work together, but nobody ever used it because it was too complicated.

sections.title: Why RFC 1403 Is Not Used
sections.content:
The BGP OSPF interaction described in RFC 1403 is not common usage in practice. The mechanism has not been observed in the public internet for many years, if ever. The complexity involved in implementation does not justify the lack of demand.

This inaction is consistent with general standards practice: when a specification remains undeployed for an extended period and shows no signs of adoption despite opportunity, it is moved to Historic status rather than kept as an active standard.
sections.eli5: No one wanted to implement this feature because it was hard and nobody needed it.

sections.title: Impact
sections.content: Moving RFC 1403 to Historic status has no known effect on the security of the internet. The mechanism was never widely deployed, so retiring it has no negative consequences for existing networks or implementations.
sections.eli5: This change does not affect how the internet works today because nobody uses this mechanism anyway.

references.text: Varadhan, K., "BGP OSPF Interaction", RFC 1403, January 1993.
